In [[mathematics]], the '''Freudenthal spectral theorem''' is a result in [[Riesz space|Riesz space theory]] proved by [[Hans Freudenthal]] in 1936. It roughly states that any  element dominated by a positive element in a [[Riesz space]] with the [[Riesz space#Projection properties|principal projection property]] can in a sense be approximated uniformly by [[simple function]]s. 

Numerous well-known results may be derived from the Freudenthal spectral theorem. The well-known [[Radon–Nikodym theorem]], the validity of the [[Poisson kernel|Poisson formula]] and the [[spectral theorem]] from the theory of [[normal operator]]s can all be shown to follow as special cases of the Freudenthal spectral theorem.

== Statement ==
Let ''e'' be any positive element in a Riesz space ''E''. A positive element of ''p'' in ''E'' is called a component of ''e'' if <math>p\wedge(e-p)=0</math>. If <math>p_1,p_2,\ldots,p_n</math> are pairwise [[Riesz_space#Disjointness|disjoint]] components of ''e'', any real linear combination of <math>p_1,p_2,\ldots,p_n</math> is called an ''e''-simple function.

The Freudenthal spectral theorem states: Let ''E'' be any Riesz space with the principal projection property and ''e'' any positive element in ''E''. Then for any element ''f'' in the principal ideal generated by ''e'', there exist sequences <math>\{s_n\}</math> and <math>\{t_n\}</math> of ''e''-simple functions, such that  <math>\{s_n\}</math> is monotone increasing and converges [[Riesz space#Order convergence|''e''-uniformly]] to ''f'', and  <math>\{t_n\}</math>  is monotone decreasing and converges ''e''-uniformly to ''f''.

== Relation to the Radon–Nikodym theorem ==
Let <math>(X,\Sigma)</math> be a [[measure space]] and <math>M_\sigma</math> the real space of [[signed measure#The space of signed measures|signed <math>\sigma</math>-additive measures]] on <math>(X,\Sigma)</math>. It can be shown that <math>M_\sigma</math> is a [[Dedekind complete]] [[Banach lattice|Banach Lattice]] with the [[total variation norm]], and hence has the [[Riesz space#Projection properties|principal projection property]]. For any positive measure <math>\mu</math>, <math>\mu</math>-simple functions (as defined above) can be shown to correspond exactly to <math>\mu</math>-measurable [[simple function]]s on <math>(X,\Sigma)</math> (in the usual sense). Moreover, since by the Freudenthal spectral theorem, any measure <math>\nu</math> in the [[Riesz space#Bands and σ-Ideals|band generated]] by <math>\mu</math> can be monotonously approximated from below by <math>\mu</math>-measurable simple functions on <math>(X,\Sigma)</math>, by [[Monotone convergence theorem#Lebesgue's monotone convergence theorem|Lebesgue's monotone convergence theorem]] <math>\nu</math> can be shown to correspond to an <math>L^1(X,\Sigma,\mu)</math> function and establishes an isometric lattice isomorphism between the band generated by <math>\mu</math> and the Banach Lattice <math>L^1(X,\Sigma,\mu)</math>.
